deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1983–84 study of systems Σ of pseudolines in a (projective, disc-model) plane, and of how one pseudoline L can be moved relative to the others. Moving L produces combinatorial 'transitions' between relative positions. A transition can be a specialization, where L is pushed across a vertex t so that a 'triangle of specialization' collapses and L comes to pass through t. It can also be a generalization, where L leaves a multiple point and a triangle opens up. Each transition is recorded by an arc on L̃, the lifted or circle model of L.

The previous page defined ordinary specialization arcs. These are the bases of the union of the triangles with apex t, for a family σ of at least two consecutive crossing points on L. It then began to define exceptional specialization arcs, which arise when the apex of the chords lies on the boundary D = ∂Δ, i.e. on the line at infinity of the disc model.

This page states five facts.
(1) L can have two exceptional specialization arcs exactly when L is a 'bisectrix' of a pencil or corridor C of lines meeting at a boundary point. The drawing shows a green circle with orange pseudolines and two antipodal blue marks where lines converge. In that case there are no other specialization arcs and exactly two generalization arcs. The four arcs together are the sides of a topological polygon structure on D̃, alternating between the two types.
(2) In general, two distinct transition arcs meet only when one is an exceptional specialization arc and the other a generalization arc, and then they are adjacent, sharing an endpoint.
(3) Definitions:
- 'Arcs of inaction' are the closures of the connected components of the complement of the union of transition arcs.
- 'Transition vertices' are the endpoints of transition arcs.
- These vertices cut L̃ into 'characteristic arcs' (the sides of characteristic polygons) of three types: generalization, specialization (ordinary or exceptional), and inaction.
- An inaction arc lies 'between' successive transition processes from one relative position to another.
(4) Adjacency lemma. With no exceptional specialization arc, of any two adjacent characteristic arcs exactly one is an inaction arc, so inaction and transition arcs alternate. Two inaction arcs are never adjacent. If two adjacent characteristic arcs are both transition arcs, one is exceptional specialization and the other generalization.
(5) The page begins a degenerate case where C reduces to a single vertex. The next page handles it by 'retracting' exceptional specialization arcs slightly, so that all transition arcs become pairwise disjoint and the alternation holds without exceptions.

Purpose: a combinatorial description of the local moves of one pseudoline relative to a fixed arrangement. This is essentially a description of the cells and adjacencies of the space of positions or extensions of L, in preparation for the generalization/specialization operation on the next page.
errors: The 'iff' characterization of when two exceptional specialization arcs occur is asserted without proof, and the term rendered 'coulisse' (pencil/corridor) is not defined on this page.

The alternation statement fails in the degenerate case where C reduces to a vertex (two transition arcs share an endpoint). Grothendieck flags this himself and repairs it on the next page by retracting the exceptional arcs. As stated here it is therefore provisional, not an error.

ideas.what: Classification of arcs on a pseudoline L into transition arcs (specialization/generalization) and complementary 'inaction' arcs, describing the elementary moves of L relative to a fixed arrangement
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of single-element extensions / extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid; triangle flips (Ringel mutations) involving one pseudoline
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flips; Las Vergnas (1978) for single-element extensions of oriented matroids; Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) for extension spaces

ideas.what: Exceptional specialization arcs arising when the apex of a pencil lies at infinity, and L 'bisecting' such a pencil giving an alternating 4-gon of transition arcs
ideas.modern_name: Mutations at the line at infinity / affine vs. projective arrangement degenerations

ideas.what: Adjacency lemma: inaction arcs and transition arcs alternate along L̃; adjacent transition arcs occur only as an exceptional-specialization/generalization pair
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial lemma on the cell structure of the position space of one pseudoline

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but essentially routine combinatorial bookkeeping on the moves of one pseudoline in an arrangement. It is close in spirit to known work on mutations and extension spaces of oriented matroids. It belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished pseudoline program but contains no evident result absent from the later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'd'une alternation de polygone topologique' — the image more plausibly reads 'd'une structure de polygone topologique sur D̃'.
'coulisse de C' — uncertain; possibly 'couloir de C' (a pencil/corridor of lines meeting at a boundary point, cf. the blue marks in the drawing).

'on peut dire[?] arcs caractéristiques adjacents, un est un seul est un arc d'inaction' should read roughly 'on peut dire : de deux arcs caractéristiques adjacents, un et un seul est un arc d'inaction'.
'Mieux,' at the end of the left column precedes a struck word and 'on appellera sommets de transition' on the right column; the 'arcs d'inaction' definition is thus restated more precisely.
